name = 'Berlin Office' kept from the benchmark check verify_two_cis_registered (which joins on l.name); not fixed by request or policy, which say 'our Berlin office'
org_id ORG_001 is the acting user's organisation (Marcus Thompson, USER_001); state not stated and not tested

the existing Sophie Mueller (USER_008, acme.com, ORG_002) is a different person; no tool in the list can update her

requirements.text: add the three agents as group members
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user_group_member WHERE group_id = 'GROUP_005' AND user_id IN ('USER_008', 'USER_009')
assumptions: boundary of the selector: Sophie Mueller (USER_008) and Kenji Tanaka (USER_009, both acme.com, ORG_002) share surnames with the new hires and could be found by a get_user_using_name lookup; they are not the three agents and must not be added
disagreement: A only (B wrote a stay on the users rows of USER_008 and USER_009 instead); kept because add_new_group_member is the one listed tool through which a surname lookup could pull them in

notes: Every row the task creates is new on the seed, so all creates have seed_count 0. Rows are anchored by id only where the task creates one row in the table (location LOC_004, user_group GROUP_005); the four users, three memberships and two CIs are selected by natural key (email, group plus user, serial number), with user ids resolved by email subqueries. Every user requirement tests location_id = 'LOC_004' because the request places all four people at the Berlin office; the benchmark does not test it. The benchmark's check 3 phrase (user_name = 'sarah.mueller' OR user_name IS NOT NULL) reduces to NOT NULL on a NOT NULL column, so user_name is not a cell. The location name 'Berlin Office' is the benchmark's prior (check 7's join) and is the one cell the request leaves open that the file still fixes. The seed's user_role table is not tested: 'manager' and 'agents' map to users.role, which the benchmark tests, and no listed tool names user_role. All creates have a tool (add_location, add_new_user, add_new_user_group, add_new_group_member, register_configuration_item). Both passes found the same twelve creates with the same cells and kept all eight original checks; they differ only in the boundary stay. disagreement: membership stay on GROUP_005 for USER_008 and USER_009: A only; kept because add_new_group_member is listed and a surname lookup could add the wrong person. disagreement: users stay keeping USER_008 and USER_009's email and org: B only; dropped because no listed tool updates an existing user (add_new_user, get_user, get_user_using_name only), so the count cannot change and the stay adds length without strictness.
